Wan Xiang 萬祥 (native of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, of civilian household registration; an Added Student of the Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Zaidao, first in his generation; aged thirty, born on the second day of the eighth month). title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟國家建官共
理天事以安生民必求真
才實德用圖成績論者咸
謂培養貴有素選舉貴有
方考課貴嚴明今兹三者
===
亦嘗修舉而百官有司未
能盡得人何歟三代以上
稽諸經可見若漢唐宋願
治之君皆知以求賢為務
而得人之盛獨稱虞周何

方考課貴嚴明今茲三者
===
亦嘗修舉而百官有司未
能盡得人何歟三代以上
稽諸經可見若漢唐宋顧
治之君皆知以求賢爲務
而得人之盛獨稱虞周何
punctuated: 皇帝制曰：「朕惟國家建官，共理天事，以安生民，必求真才實德，用圖成績。論者咸謂培養貴有素，選舉貴有方，考課貴嚴明。今兹三者，亦嘗修舉，而百官有司未能盡得人，何歟？三代以上，稽諸經可見。若漢、唐、宋願治之君，皆知以求賢為務，而得人之盛獨稱虞、周，何
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: "We reflect that when the state establishes offices to jointly administer the affairs of Heaven so as to bring peace to the people, it must seek out genuine talent and solid virtue in order to achieve successful governance. Commentators all say that in nurturing talent, what is valued is steady preparation beforehand; in selection and appointment, what is valued is proper method; and in performance evaluation, what is valued is strictness and clarity. At present, these three measures have indeed been instituted and practiced, yet among the hundred officials and the authorities in charge we have still not been able to obtain capable men in every case—why is this? For the Three Dynasties and earlier, one may examine the Classics to see how things stood. As for the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song who desired good governance, all knew to make the search for the worthy their priority, yet for the flourishing abundance of capable men attained, only Yu [Shun] and the Zhou are praised—why…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
歟期于濟濟多士秉文之
德九德咸事俊乂在官用
臻雍熈泰和之治果何道
以致之歟朕祗承
祖宗大統以安民為心惓惓
===
于茲久矣諸生講明治道
出膺時用必有定論其直
述以對無騁夸辭無摭陳
言朕將采而行之

德九德咸事俊乂在官用

祖宗大統以安民為心惓惓
===
于茲久矣諸生講明治道
出膺時用必有定論其直
述以對無騁奇辭無摭陳
言朕將采而行之
punctuated: 歟？期于「濟濟多士，秉文之德」，「九德咸事，俊乂在官」，用臻雍熈泰和之治，果何道以致之歟？朕祗承祖宗大統，以安民為心，惓惓于茲久矣。諸生講明治道，出膺時用，必有定論。其直述以對，無騁夸辭，無摭陳言，朕將采而行之。
translation_en:
…is this so? If we hope to reach the state where “numerous is the array of officers, who cleave to the virtue of King Wen,” and where “the men of the nine virtues all serve, and the eminent and able are in office,” thereby attaining an era of harmonious and prosperous peace and order, by what way can this truly be brought about?

We have reverently succeeded to the great legitimacy of Our Imperial Ancestors, taking the pacification of the people as Our heart’s concern, and have been earnestly devoted to this for a long time now. You students have studied and elucidated the Way of governance and are coming forth to answer the needs of the age, so you must have settled views on this. Set them forth straightforwardly in your replies; do not indulge in boastful rhetoric, and do not merely gather up stale clichés, for We shall select from your words and put them into practice.

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
臣劉儼
臣對臣聞孔子曰為政在人取人以身脩身以
道脩道以仁大哉人君之一身乎其為取人為
政之根本乎故有志於帝王之盛治者不可不
求其人有志於帝王之用人者不可不脩其身
其身既脩則所以培養人材於未用之先選擧
人材於將用之際而考課於既用之後無往而
不宜矣尚何患乎真材實德之不可得而唐虞
三代之不可及哉欽惟
陛下聰明先物睿知有臨心二帝三王之要道紹
===
祖宗列聖之宏規即位以来孜孜求賢以圖至治其
得人之盛致治之美蓋無以加矣而尤發
綸音下明詔首以
國家用人之方次及虞周得人之盛下詢微賤以
求定論臣有以知
陛下誠大有為之君也其所以復隆古之至治開萬
世之太平端在此矣臣敢不悉心以對竊惟天
生斯民不能自治故必命之君君撫斯民不能
獨治故必任之臣是臣之所以為臣非徒取其
充位而已也備員而已也食君之祿而已也上

===
祖宗列聖之宏規即位以來孜孜求賢以圖至治其
得人之盛致治之美蓋無以加矣而尤發
綸音下明詔首以
國家用人之方次及虞周得人之盛下詢微賤以
求定論臣有以知
陛下誠大有爲之君也其所以復隆古之至治開萬
世之太平端在此矣臣敢不悉心以對竊惟天
生斯民不能自治故必命之君君撫斯民不能
獨治故必任之臣是臣之所以爲臣非徒取其
充位而已也備員而已也食君之禄而已也上
punctuated:
臣劉儼。
臣對：臣聞孔子曰：「為政在人，取人以身，脩身以道，脩道以仁。」大哉，人君之一身乎！其為取人為政之根本乎！故有志於帝王之盛治者，不可不求其人；有志於帝王之用人者，不可不脩其身。其身既脩，則所以培養人材於未用之先，選擧人材於將用之際，而考課於既用之後，無往而不宜矣。尚何患乎真材實德之不可得，而唐、虞、三代之不可及哉！欽惟陛下聰明先物，睿知有臨，心二帝、三王之要道，紹祖宗列聖之宏規，即位以来，孜孜求賢，以圖至治。其得人之盛，致治之美，蓋無以加矣。而尤發綸音，下明詔，首以國家用人之方，次及虞、周得人之盛，下詢微賤，以求定論。臣有以知陛下誠大有為之君也，其所以復隆古之至治、開萬世之太平，端在此矣。臣敢不悉心以對！竊惟天生斯民，不能自治，故必命之君；君撫斯民，不能獨治，故必任之臣。是臣之所以為臣，非徒取其充位而已也，備員而已也，食君之祿而已也。上
translation_en:
Your servant Liu Yan 劉儼.
Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that Confucius 孔子 said: "Governance lies in men; men are obtained by means of the ruler's own person; the person is cultivated by means of the Way; the Way is cultivated by means of benevolence." Great indeed is the single person of the sovereign! Is it not the fundamental root of obtaining men and conducting governance? Therefore, one who aspires to the flourishing governance of the emperors and kings of old cannot but seek out the right men; and one who aspires to the way those emperors and kings employed men cannot but cultivate his own person. Once his person is cultivated, then in nurturing talent before it is employed, selecting talent when it is about to be employed, and evaluating its performance after it has been employed, there will be nothing that is not fitting. What worry would there still be that men of genuine talent and solid virtue could not be obtained, or that the eras of Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and the Three Dynasties could not be equaled!
I reverently reflect that Your Majesty, with acute perception that anticipates affairs and sagely wisdom suited to rule, takes to heart the essential Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and continues the grand design of Your Ancestors and the successive Sacred Emperors. Since ascending the throne, You have tirelessly sought out the worthy in order to plan for supreme governance. The abundance of talent You have obtained and the beauty of the order You have achieved truly cannot be surpassed. Yet You still issue Your silken words and send down a clear edict, asking first about the Dynasty's methods of employing men, and next about the abundance of talent obtained in the eras of Yu and Zhou 周, inquiring down to the humble and lowly in search of a settled conclusion. By this, your servant knows that Your Majesty is truly a ruler of great enterprise, and that the means to restore the supreme governance of high antiquity and open up universal peace for ten thousand generations lies squarely in this. How could your servant dare not exhaust his heart in reply!
I humbly reflect that when Heaven gives birth to this people, they cannot govern themselves, and therefore Heaven must appoint a ruler for them; when the ruler cherishes this people, he cannot govern them alone, and therefore he must entrust office to ministers. Thus, that by which a minister is a minister is not merely that he is taken to fill a post, merely to make up the numbers, or merely to eat the ruler's emolument. Above, …

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
而天事以之而共理下而生民以之而共安自
非真材實德之士鮮有不瘝官而曠職者矣洪
惟
國朝
聖聖相承丕圖治理以養賢必本於學校也內置國
子監以教天下之英材外設府州縣學以育民
間之俊秀既擇師儒以專其職又命憲臣以董
其綱迄今七十餘年教化之功愈久而愈盛此
其培養可謂有素矣以用賢必資於科目也或
由進士舉或由胄監選或以賢良方正為名或
===
以材德兼備為科取賢任材類非一途此其選
舉可謂有方矣以至三年而一考九年而通考
善良者陞之賞之回邪者黜之罪之其考課之
法又不可謂不嚴且明矣然而百官有司未盡
得人者豈用是三者而不效哉亦以徒徇其名
而不求其實之過也臣請稽諸古揆諸今為
陛下陳之夫唐虞三代之世其培養之制有小學以
為大學之根本有大學以收小學之成功自愛
親敬長之事以馴致夫明德新民之功而天子
公卿躬行於上言行政事皆可師法此其養之

punctuated: 而天事以之而共理，下而生民以之而共安。自非真材實德之士，鮮有不瘝官而曠職者矣。洪惟國朝，聖聖相承，丕圖治理。以養賢必本於學校也，內置國子監以教天下之英材，外設府、州、縣學以育民間之俊秀；既擇師儒以專其職，又命憲臣以董其綱，迄今七十餘年，教化之功愈久而愈盛，此其培養可謂有素矣。以用賢必資於科目也，或由進士舉，或由胄監選，或以賢良方正為名，或以材德兼備為科，取賢任材，類非一途，此其選舉可謂有方矣。以至三年而一考，九年而通考，善良者陞之、賞之，回邪者黜之、罪之，其考課之法，又不可謂不嚴且明矣。然而百官有司未盡得人者，豈用是三者而不效哉？亦以徒徇其名而不求其實之過也。臣請稽諸古、揆諸今，為陛下陳之。夫唐、虞、三代之世，其培養之制，有小學以為大學之根本，有大學以收小學之成功；自愛親敬長之事，以馴致夫明德新民之功，而天子、公卿躬行於上，言行政事，皆可師法，此其養之
translation_en: …above, the affairs of Heaven are thereby jointly ordered; below, the common people are thereby jointly given peace. Unless they are scholars of genuine talent and true virtue, few will fail to neglect their offices and derelict their duties. Looking upon our reigning dynasty in its greatness, sage has succeeded sage in grandly planning for good governance. Holding that the nurturing of the worthy must be rooted in schools, within the capital it established the Directorate of Education (Guozijian) to instruct the outstanding talents of the realm, and in the provinces it instituted prefectural, subprefectural, and county schools to cultivate the promising youths among the people. Having selected Confucian teachers to devote themselves exclusively to their duties, it also commissioned censorial officials to supervise the overall system. Now, after more than seventy years, the achievements of education and transformation have grown ever more flourishing with the passage of time; thus, its cultivation of talent may well be called well-established. Holding that the employment of the worthy must rely upon examination categories, some are recommended as metropolitan graduates (jinshi), some are selected from the Directorate of Education, some are nominated under the title of "Worthy and Good, Square and Upright," and some are categorized as "Possessing Both Talent and Virtue." The selection of the worthy and the appointment of the talented generally do not follow a single path; thus, its recruitment and selection may well be called methodical. Furthermore, there is an evaluation every three years and a comprehensive evaluation after nine years: the upright and good are promoted and rewarded, while the devious and wicked are dismissed and punished; thus, its system of performance evaluation cannot be called anything less than strict and clear. And yet, the various offices and authorities have not completely succeeded in obtaining the right men—could it be that employing these three measures is ineffective? It is rather the fault of merely pursuing the name without seeking the reality. Your servant begs leave to examine antiquity and measure the present, and to set this forth for Your Majesty. In the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, under their system of cultivation, there was the Lesser Learning to serve as the foundation for the Greater Learning, and the Greater Learning to bring to fruition the accomplishments of the Lesser Learning. Proceeding from the duties of loving one's parents and respecting one's elders, they gradually attained the achievement of manifesting illustrious virtue and renewing the people; meanwhile, the Son of Heaven and the ducal ministers practiced these principles personally from above, so that their words, deeds, and administrative affairs could all serve as models. Thus, in their nurturing of men…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
於學也有其實而非虛名之徇矣其選舉之方
敷納以言然後明庶以功明庶以功然後車服
以庸未嘗輕易以舉之既宅三宅以任其事又
儲三俊以備其選未嘗造次而用之此其舉之
於朝也有其實而非虛名之徇矣至於三載考
績三考黜陟幽明與夫歲終各正其治而廢置
之三歲大計其治而誅賞之此其課試之者又
豈務虛名而不求其實哉是以求之當時濟濟
多士秉文之德九德咸事俊乂在官信有如詩
書之所言矣然原其所以致此者何莫不自聖
===
人脩身為之本哉三代而下若漢唐宋願治之
君固皆以得賢為務然考之於史以言其教人
或尊師重傅或大召名儒六學之有領三舍之
有生名則美矣其視唐虞三代之躬行心得者
為何如以言其舉人賢良之有科孝廉之有舉
六科四事之辟三經十科之制名則嘉矣其視
唐虞三代之敷言奏功克用宅俊者為何若至
若考課之法有尚書以典公卿二千石曹尚書
以典郡國三銓之有法循資之有格又可與唐
虞三代考績黜陟之典並論哉是則漢唐宋養

…in the schools possessed true substance and was not a mere pursuit of empty names. As for their methods of selection and promotion, candidates presented their views in words and were received, after which they were clearly tested through their achievements; once they were clearly tested through their achievements, they were rewarded with carriages and vestments to employ them—they were never promoted lightly. Having placed men in the three appointed positions to take charge of affairs, the rulers also kept in reserve men of the three grades of preeminent talent to prepare for future selection—they never employed anyone hastily. Thus, their promotion of men at court possessed true substance and was not a mere pursuit of empty names. As for examining merits every three years and demoting the incompetent and promoting the enlightened after three examinations, as well as rectifying the administration of each official at the end of the year to dismiss or retain them, and conducting a grand reckoning of their governance every three years to punish or reward them—in testing and evaluating officials in this way, how could they have pursued empty names without seeking true substance? Therefore, if we look at those times, "the multitude of finest officers held fast to the virtue of King Wen," and "men of the nine virtues all served, with eminent talents in office"—it was truly just as described in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu). Yet if we trace the reason why this was achieved, how could any of it not have taken the sage's cultivation of his own person as its foundation!

From the Three Dynasties downward, rulers of Han, Tang, and Song who desired good governance certainly all made obtaining worthy men their priority. Yet if we examine the histories, to speak of how they educated men: whether honoring teachers and esteeming tutors, or summoning renowned Confucians on a grand scale, having directors in charge of the Six Academies, or having students in the Three Halls—the names were indeed fine, but how did they compare to the personal practice and inward attainment of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? To speak of how they selected men: having the category of Worthy and Excellent, the recommendation of Filial and Incorrupt, recruitment by the Six Categories and Four Qualifications, and the systems of the Three Classics and Ten Categories—the names were indeed admirable, but how did they compare to presenting words and demonstrating achievements, and being able to employ those in the appointed positions and men of preeminent talent in Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? And as for their methods of performance evaluation: having Imperial Secretaries (Shangshu) in charge of the Excellencies and Ministers, Imperial Secretaries of the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau in charge of commanderies and kingdoms, the regulations of the Three Selections, and the qualification scales of seniority—how could these be discussed in the same breath as the canons of examining merits and demoting or promoting in Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
士取士之法既皆不能如唐虞三代之本於脩
身以務其實則其成人得人之效又豈能比隆
唐虞三代之盛哉今
陛下期於得人必曰秉文曰九德期於致治必曰雍
煕泰和臣有以知
陛下心堯舜禹湯文武之心矣
陛下既心乎堯舜禹湯文武之心則其所以興學校
慎選舉嚴考課舍唐虞三代其何以為法哉臣
伏覩
陛下興學校以作成天下之士類亦云至矣然而師
===
之所以教弟子之所以學率從事於文藝之末
不務以德行為本故鮮有所成就此臣願
陛下脩身以端教化之本如唐虞三代之君則即所
謂上有好者下必有甚焉者矣
陛下設選舉以網羅天下之賢俊亦云廣矣然舉賢
良者或竊賢良之名稱材德者或乏材德之實
故不能皆稱任使此臣願
陛下脩身以為知人之要如唐虞三代之君則即所
謂允迪厥德謨明弼諧矣至於考課之法所以
勸善而懲怠比年以來典是任者惟知體

謂允迪厥德謨明弼諧矣至於考課之法所以
勸善而懲怠比年以來典是任者惟知體
punctuated: 士、取士之法，既皆不能如唐、虞、三代之本於脩身以務其實，則其成人、得人之效，又豈能比隆唐、虞、三代之盛哉！今陛下期於得人，必曰「秉文」，曰「九德」；期於致治，必曰「雍煕」、「泰和」。臣有以知陛下心堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心矣。陛下既心乎堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心，則其所以興學校、慎選舉、嚴考課，舍唐、虞、三代，其何以為法哉？臣伏覩陛下興學校以作成天下之士類，亦云至矣。然而師之所以教、弟子之所以學，率從事於文藝之末，不務以德行為本，故鮮有所成就。此臣願陛下脩身以端教化之本，如唐、虞、三代之君，則即所謂「上有好者，下必有甚焉者」矣。陛下設選舉以網羅天下之賢俊，亦云廣矣。然舉賢良者或竊賢良之名，稱材德者或乏材德之實，故不能皆稱任使。此臣願陛下脩身以為知人之要，如唐、虞、三代之君，則即所謂「允迪厥德，謨明弼諧」矣。至於考課之法，所以勸善而懲怠。比年以來，典是任者惟知體
translation_en:
… [nurturing] scholars and selecting scholars could none of them match those of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties in being rooted in self-cultivation so as to attend to substantive reality, how then could their efficacy in perfecting men and obtaining men rival the flourishing heights of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties?

Now, when Your Majesty aspires to obtain men of talent, You invariably speak of "upholding the civil virtue" and of the "Nine Virtues"; when You aspire to bring about good governance, You invariably speak of "harmonious splendour" and "supreme peace." From this Your servant knows that Your Majesty takes as Your own mind the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Since Your Majesty takes as Your mind the mind of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, then in the means by which You promote schools, exercise care in selection and recommendation, and strictly enforce personnel evaluation, if You set aside Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, what else could You take as a model?

Your servant humbly observes that in promoting schools to mould and perfect the scholars of the realm, Your Majesty has indeed gone to the utmost. And yet, what teachers teach and what disciples study is generally devoted to the superficialities of literary skill, without striving to take moral conduct as the foundation; therefore, few achieve true accomplishment. In view of this, Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would cultivate Your person so as to rectify the foundation of transformative teaching, just like the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—which is precisely what is meant by the saying, "What the superior loves, those below will surely pursue even more."

In establishing the system of selection and recommendation to gather in the worthy and eminent men of the realm, Your Majesty has indeed cast a wide net. Yet those recommended as "worthy and upright" sometimes usurp the mere name of worthiness and uprightness, and those praised for "talent and virtue" sometimes lack the reality of talent and virtue, so that they cannot all prove equal to their appointments. In view of this, Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would cultivate Your person as the essential key to knowing men, just like the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—which is precisely what is meant by the saying, "If the sovereign sincerely pursues his virtue, the counsels will be enlightened and the aids harmonious."

As for the methods of personnel evaluation, they are the means to encourage goodness and punish negligence. In recent years, however, those in charge of this responsibility have only known how to embody …

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
□□□厚之德不務嚴黜陟之法故勸懲□□□
典臣願
陛下脩身以正激勸之原如唐虞三代之君則即所
謂惟仁者能好人能惡人矣
陛下於是三者誠能本之以脩身遠宗唐虞三代聖
人之道近守
祖宗列聖之法斟酌而行之則内而
朝廷外而四方郡邑舉皆賢者在位能者在職又
何未盡得人之足慮哉
陛下之策臣者前既陳之矣而於終篇又策之曰
===
朕祗承
祖宗大統以安民為心惓惓于兹久矣臣又以見
陛下視民如傷求賢如渴之心也然人之一心操舍
無定久則易怠要必貴於有常天有常故不息
地有常故載厚日月有常故久照
陛下中天地而立並日月之明必體其有常之運以
之脩身以之求賢以之愛民廣堂如是深宫如
是大政大事如是微言細行如是則即伊尹所
謂常厥德保厥位矣天下幸甚生民幸甚臣學
不足以明治道材不足以膺時用惟因

上〔臣〕顧

何未盡得人之足慮哉
陛下之策〔臣〕者前既陳之矣而於終篇又策之曰
===
朕祇承
祖宗大統以安民為心惓惓于茲久矣〔臣〕又以見
陛下視民如傷求賢如渴也〔臣〕〔臣〕然人之一心操舍
無定久則易怠要必貴於有常天有常故不息

之脩身以之求賢以之愛民廣堂如是深宮如

punctuated: □□□厚之德，不務嚴黜陟之法，故勸懲□□□典。臣願陛下脩身以正激勸之原，如唐、虞、三代之君，則即所謂「惟仁者能好人，能惡人」矣。陛下於是三者，誠能本之以脩身，遠宗唐、虞、三代聖人之道，近守祖宗列聖之法，斟酌而行之，則内而朝廷，外而四方郡邑，舉皆賢者在位，能者在職，又何未盡得人之足慮哉！陛下之策臣者，前既陳之矣，而於終篇又策之曰：「朕祗承祖宗大統，以安民為心，惓惓于兹久矣。」臣又以見陛下視民如傷、求賢如渴之心也。然人之一心，操舍無定，久則易怠，要必貴於有常。天有常故不息，地有常故載厚，日月有常故久照。陛下中天地而立，並日月之明，必體其有常之運，以之脩身，以之求賢，以之愛民。廣堂如是，深宫如是；大政大事如是，微言細行如是。則即伊尹所謂「常厥德，保厥位」矣。天下幸甚，生民幸甚。臣學不足以明治道，材不足以膺時用，惟因…
translation_en:
…[embody Your Majesty's gen]erous [?] virtue, and do not strive to strictly enforce the laws of demotion and promotion; thus encouragement and punishment [lack a regular?] standard. Your servant wishes that Your Majesty would cultivate your person in order to rectify the source of stimulation and encouragement, like the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; then this will be what is meant by the saying, "Only the benevolent person can love others and can hate others." If in these three matters Your Majesty can truly root them in personal cultivation, distantly taking as your model the Way of the sages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and closely upholding the laws of the imperial ancestors and successive sage emperors, deliberating upon them and putting them into practice, then within at the imperial court and without across the prefectures and counties of the four quarters, all will have the worthy in office and the capable in their posts—what need would there be to worry about not having completely obtained the right men!

That upon which Your Majesty has questioned your servant, I have already set forth above. Yet at the end of your inquiry, you further question us, saying: "We have reverently succeeded to the great line of Our Imperial Ancestors, taking the pacification of the people as Our mind, and have been earnestly devoted to this for a long time." From this, your servant further perceives Your Majesty's heart that looks upon the people as if they were wounded and seeks the worthy as if thirsting. However, a person's single mind has no fixed constancy in what it holds fast and what it lets go; over time it easily grows lax, so the essential thing must lie in valuing constancy. Heaven has constancy, and therefore never ceases; Earth has constancy, and therefore supports all things with its thickness; the sun and moon have constancy, and therefore shine enduringly. Your Majesty stands centered between Heaven and Earth and matches the brightness of the sun and moon; you must embody their constant revolutions, using this constancy to cultivate your person, using it to seek the worthy, and using it to love the people. Be thus in the broad audience hall, and be thus in the deep palace; be thus in great governance and major affairs, and be thus in subtle words and minor conduct. Then this will be what Yi Yin 伊尹 meant by saying, "Be constant in your virtue, to preserve your throne." How fortunate for the realm! How fortunate for the living people! Your servant's learning is insufficient to illuminate the way of governance, and my talent is insufficient to meet the needs of the times; only because…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
聖問所及謹直述以對若夫騁夸辭以取容摭陳言
之無益則非臣之志也惟
陛下憫其愚而擇焉臣謹對
alt_text:
聖問所及謹〔古〕述以對若夫騁夸辭以取容摭陳言
之無益則非〔臣〕之志也惟
陛下憫其愚而擇焉〔臣〕謹對
punctuated: 聖問所及，謹直述以對。若夫騁夸辭以取容，摭陳言之無益，則非臣之志也。惟陛下憫其愚而擇焉。臣謹對。
translation_en: … what Your Sacred Inquiry touches upon, I respectfully and straightforwardly set forth my reply. As for indulging in boastful rhetoric to curry favor or gathering stale words of no benefit, that is not your servant's intent. May Your Majesty take pity on my foolishness and select from what I have offered. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
臣呂原
臣對臣聞人君欲求安民之效莫先於用賢欲
盡用賢之實尤在於法古蓋賢才乃致治之本
必其養之有素取之有術勸懲之有道如古帝
王躬行之盡其實則真才可得庶職可備而天
事以治生民以安何患不臻於隆古之治哉故
後世欲追唐虞三代之治者不可不以唐虞三
代帝王之道為法也書曰監于先王成憲其永
無愆詩曰不愆不忘率由舊章蓋謂是已恭惟
皇上備乾剛中正之德履九五至尊之位臨御以来
===
宵旰惓惓惟以奉
天圖治為心而凡求賢安民亦惟帝王與
祖宗之道是循是用於學校之教則既擇師儒以訓
之又分命憲臣以董之而培養之功已至科目
之設則求實才以汰浮華嚴解額以杜僥倖而
選舉之道已精屢降
綸音諄諄戒飭罷黜貪懦登進賢能而考課之法
已詳斯三者固無一之不備舉由是下無遺才
上無廢事而得人致治之效亦已至矣
皇上不自滿足猶以為百官有司未盡得人必欲正

===
天圖治為心而凡求賢安民亦惟帝王與
祖宗之道是循是用於學校之教則既擇師儒以訓
之又分命憲臣以董之而培養之功已至科目
之設則求實才以汰浮華嚴解額以杜僥倖而
選舉之道已精屢降
綸音諄諄戒飭罷黜貪儒登進賢能而考課之法
已詳斯三者固無一之不脩舉由是下無遺才
上無廢事而得人致治之效亦已至矣
皇上不自滿足猶以為百官有司未盡得人必欲止
punctuated:
臣呂原。

臣對：臣聞人君欲求安民之效，莫先於用賢；欲盡用賢之實，尤在於法古。蓋賢才乃致治之本，必其養之有素，取之有術，勸懲之有道，如古帝王躬行之，盡其實，則真才可得，庶職可備，而天事以治，生民以安，何患不臻於隆古之治哉？故後世欲追唐、虞、三代之治者，不可不以唐、虞、三代帝王之道為法也。《書》曰：「監于先王成憲，其永無愆。」《詩》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」蓋謂是已。

恭惟皇上備乾剛中正之德，履九五至尊之位，臨御以来，宵旰惓惓，惟以奉天圖治為心；而凡求賢安民，亦惟帝王與祖宗之道是循是用。於學校之教，則既擇師儒以訓之，又分命憲臣以董之，而培養之功已至；科目之設，則求實才以汰浮華，嚴解額以杜僥倖，而選舉之道已精；屢降綸音，諄諄戒飭，罷黜貪懦，登進賢能，而考課之法已詳。斯三者，固無一之不備舉，由是下無遺才，上無廢事，而得人致治之效亦已至矣。皇上不自滿足，猶以為百官有司未盡得人，必欲正
translation_en:
Your servant Lü Yuan 呂原.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that if a ruler wishes to seek the efficacy of bringing peace to the people, nothing takes precedence over employing the worthy; and if he wishes to fulfill the substance of employing the worthy, it lies above all in emulating antiquity. For worthy talent is the foundation of achieving good governance. Only when there is a steady foundation in nurturing them, a method in selecting them, and a proper way in encouraging and admonishing them—practiced personally and fulfilled in substance as the emperors and kings of antiquity did—can true talent be obtained and the various offices be fully staffed. Then Heaven's work [?] will be ordered and the people will be at peace; what worry would there be of not attaining the flourishing governance of high antiquity? Therefore, those in later generations who wish to match the governance of Tang 唐 [Yao], Yu 虞 [Shun], and the Three Dynasties cannot but take the way of the emperors and kings of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties as their model. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Take as your mirror the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without fault." The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Neither erring nor forgetting, following the old statutes." This is indeed what is meant.

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty possesses the virtue of Heaven's firmness, centrality, and correctness, and occupies the supreme position of the Nine-in-the-Fifth. Since ascending the throne, from before dawn until late at night you have been earnestly devoted, taking solely the service of Heaven and the pursuit of good governance as your heart's concern; and in all matters of seeking the worthy and bringing peace to the people, you likewise follow and employ solely the way of the ancient emperors and kings and the Imperial Ancestors. Regarding instruction in the schools, you have both selected Confucian teachers to train the students and separately commissioned Censorial Officials to supervise them, so that the work of cultivation is already complete. Regarding the institution of the examination categories, you seek substantive talent so as to weed out superficial ostentation, and strictly enforce provincial quotas so as to close off opportunistic advancement, so that the way of selection is already refined. And you have repeatedly handed down silken decrees, earnestly and tirelessly admonishing and warning, dismissing the corrupt and cowardly while advancing the worthy and capable, so that the methods of personnel evaluation are already thorough. Of these three things, there is truly not one that is not fully instituted and carried out. Consequently, below there is no overlooked talent, above there are no neglected affairs, and the efficacy of obtaining men and achieving good governance has already reached its utmost. Yet Your Majesty is not self-satisfied, still considering that the hundred officials and the authorities have not been entirely filled with the right men, and 반드시 desiring to [rectify? / directly?] …

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
追虞周之盛惓惓于兹為言乃進臣等於
廷虚心賜問責以定論臣雖愚昧竊有以知
皇上是心即古帝王制治保邦不遑寧處之盛心也
臣敢不拜手稽首以對揚
明命之萬一夫惟天惠民而必立之君惟辟奉天而
必任之臣是人君之用賢實所以為天下生民
計也然必教養選任勸懲之盡其道則所用皆
真才實德而天人之責庶幾兼盡而無曠焉粤
稽諸古唐虞建官惟百内有百揆四岳外有州
牧侯伯為之制禮作樂共代天工都俞戒勅臣
===
隣賛襄當時庶政惟和萬國咸寧果何以致此
哉由其惇典敷教翕受敷施以培養選舉於其
前奏言試功考績黜陟而嚴考課於其後也成
周建官仰惟前代時若大而三公三孤次而六
卿九牧為之經邦弘化分職率属上下相維體
統不紊當時兆民阜成萬邦咸休亦何以致此
哉由其塾庠序學之設大比賓興之制以培養
選舉於其前歳終受會三歳大計群吏之弊而
行考課於其後也三代而下漢唐宋之君有志
於治者未甞不以求賢為務然漢有孝弟力田

追虞、周之盛，惓惓于兹為言，乃進臣等於廷，虚心賜問，責以定論。臣雖愚昧，竊有以知皇上是心，即古帝王制治保邦、不遑寧處之盛心也。臣敢不拜手稽首，以對揚明命之萬一？
夫惟天惠民而必立之君，惟辟奉天而必任之臣，是人君之用賢，實所以為天下生民計也。然必教養、選任、勸懲之盡其道，則所用皆真才實德，而天人之責庶幾兼盡而無曠焉。粤稽諸古：唐、虞建官惟百，内有百揆、四岳，外有州牧、侯伯，為之制禮作樂，共代天工，都俞戒勅，臣隣賛襄，當時庶政惟和，萬國咸寧。果何以致此哉？由其惇典敷教、翕受敷施，以培養選舉於其前；奏言試功、考績黜陟，而嚴考課於其後也。成周建官，仰惟前代時若，大而三公、三孤，次而六卿、九牧，為之經邦弘化、分職率属，上下相維，體統不紊，當時兆民阜成，萬邦咸休。亦何以致此哉？由其塾、庠、序、學之設，大比賓興之制，以培養選舉於其前；歳終受會、三歳大計群吏之弊，而行考課於其後也。
三代而下，漢、唐、宋之君有志於治者，未甞不以求賢為務。然漢有孝弟力田、
translation_en:
…emulate the flourishing eras of Yu and Zhou, speaking earnestly of this matter, and thus have summoned your servants to the court, asking questions with an open mind and charging us to offer definitive arguments. Though your servant is foolish and ignorant, I venture to recognize that this intention of Your Majesty is none other than the grand intention of the emperors and kings of antiquity, who established order and preserved the state without ever allowing themselves a moment of idle rest. How dare your servant not bow with clasped hands and touch my head to the ground to respond to and extol even one ten-thousandth of Your enlightened mandate?

Now, because Heaven cherishes the people, it must establish a ruler for them; because the sovereign serves Heaven, he must employ ministers. Thus, a ruler's employment of the worthy is truly undertaken for the sake of all the living people of the realm. Yet only when the ways of education and nurturing, selection and appointment, and encouragement and chastisement are fully exhausted will those employed all be men of true talent and genuine virtue, so that the responsibilities owed to Heaven and humanity may perhaps both be fulfilled without neglect.

Examining antiquity: Tang and Yu established a hundred offices; within the court there were the General Regulator and the Four Mountains, and outside there were the Pastors of the Provinces and the regional lords and earls. They instituted rites and created music, jointly carrying out Heaven's work; with exclamations of approval and mutual admonitions, the ministerial neighbors assisted and supported the sovereign. At that time, the numerous affairs of government were harmonious and all the myriad states were at peace. How indeed was this brought about? It was because they upheld the five relationships and spread instruction, and broadly received talents and put them to work, thereby nurturing and selecting them beforehand; and they had officials present reports and tested them by their achievements, evaluating their merits to demote the unworthy and promote the worthy, thereby strictly conducting performance evaluations afterward.

When perfected Zhou established its offices, it looked up to emulate the former dynasties: at the highest level were the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries, and next were the Six Ministers and Nine Pastors. For the ruler they ordered the state and broadened the transforming influence, and divided duties to lead their subordinates. Superiors and inferiors were bound together, and the hierarchical system was unconfused. At that time, the millions of people prospered and matured, and the myriad states all enjoyed blessings. How, too, was this brought about? It was through the establishment of village, community, district, and state schools, and the institution of the triennial examination and the presentation of worthy guests, by which they nurtured and selected them beforehand; and by receiving annual accounts at the end of the year and conducting the great triennial audit of the conduct of all the officials, by which they carried out performance evaluations afterward.

From the Three Dynasties downward, the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song who aspired to good governance never failed to make seeking the worthy their priority. Yet Han had such recruitment categories as Filial and Fraternal, Diligent in Farming, …

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
賢良方正等科名則美矣其所得惟賈誼勸興
禮樂董仲舒正誼明道為可稱耳他如張禹公
孫弘阿諛之輩果可齒歟唐有秀才明經明法
明筭一史三史諸目名則嘉矣其所得惟韓愈
排斥佛老陸贄論諫仁義為足取耳他如牛僧
孺皇甫鎛奸邪之流又可數歟宋有天下育才
以學校取士以科目得人如韓范之出入將相
富歐之文章政事其餘端人碩輔類非一人宜
若幾於三代者然而君子小人迭為消長周程
張朱不獲大用其得人之實又可知矣此無他
===
帝王之世教人必以德行道藝取士必由鄉舉
里選考課必以載采采克知灼見為心而天子
公卿又皆躬行以為師法是以得人之盛誠有
如詩所謂濟濟多士秉文之德書所謂九德咸
事俊乂在官者矣迨于後世教之而無所本取
之不由其道考之不以其實為君臣者又或安
於卑近溺於利欲而不知躬行以為立教之本
是以得人之效終不能比擬於古也今
皇上急於求賢以圖治理於培養選舉考課之道固
皆行之而有其效兹又以唐虞成周為期者臣又

translation_en: … the Moral and Upright (xianliang fangzheng), and other categories; the names were indeed fine, yet among those they obtained, only Jia Yi 賈誼, who urged the revival of rites and music, and Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒, who rectified righteousness and clarified the Way, are worthy of praise. As for others like the sycophanticilk of Zhang Yu 張禹 and Gongsun Hong 公孫弘, are they really worth mentioning? The Tang had the various examination subjects of Cultivated Talent (xiucai), Classicist (mingjing), Legalist (mingfa), Mathematician (mingsuan), Single History (yishi), and Three Histories (sanshi); the names were indeed admirable, yet among those they obtained, only Han Yu 韓愈, who rejected Buddhism and Daoism, and Lu Zhi 陸贄, who remonstrated on benevolence and righteousness, are worthy of selection. As for others like the treacherous ilk of Niu Sengru 牛僧孺 and Huangfu Bo 皇甫鎛, are they even worth counting? When the Song possessed the empire, it nurtured talent through schools and selected scholars through examination categories. It obtained men such as Han Qi 韓琦 and Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, who served both as generals in the field and grand councilors at court, and Fu Bi 富弼 and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修, renowned for their literature and statecraft, while other upright men and great ministers were by no means solitary figures, so that it seemed almost to approach the Three Dynasties. Yet gentlemen and petty men waxed and waned by turns, and Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤), Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 never achieved grand employment; thus the reality of its success in obtaining men can also be known. This is for no other reason than that in the age of the Emperors and Kings, instructing men was invariably based on moral conduct, the Way, and the arts; selecting scholars invariably proceeded through district recommendation and village selection (xiangju lixuan); and evaluating performance invariably took "attending to their various deeds" and "truly knowing and clearly perceiving" as its guiding mind, while the Son of Heaven and the Dukes and Ministers all personally practiced morality to serve as teachers and models. Therefore, the flourishing of talent they obtained truly matched what the Book of Odes (Shi) calls "the眾多 multitude of scholars, holding fast to the virtue of King Wen," and what the Book of Documents (Shu) calls "when the nine virtues are all practiced in service, men of eminent talent are in office." Coming down to later ages, they instructed men without a fundamental basis, selected them without following the proper Way, and evaluated them without regard to reality. Moreover, rulers and ministers at times rested content with the base and shallow, or drowned in greed and desire, not knowing how to practice morality in person as the foundation for establishing instruction. Thus the efficacy of their obtaining men could never compare to that of antiquity. Now Your Majesty is eager to seek the worthy in order to plan for good governance, and with respect to the ways of nurturing, selecting, and evaluating, you have assuredly put them all into practice with effect; that you now further set the ages of Yao and Shun (Tang Yu) and the flourishing Zhou (Cheng Zhou) as your goal makes your servant further…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
以知
皇上此心必欲得天下真才之用而致治之效必欲
躋于雍熈泰和之盛也然虞周聖人所以致此
者豈偶然哉實由躬行以為本耳
皇上誠能取法虞周躬行教化以培養士類則必益
重師儒之選敦崇仁義之教而成人有德小子
有造之效可致矣躬行道德以選舉人才則必
益嚴主司之權務慎貢舉之法而黎獻共臣野
無遺賢之效可必矣由是立為定制以考課庶
官則必益擇銓衡之任大明黜陟之典而百工
===
惟時庶官無曠之效可期矣夫如是則賢能在
職君子盈朝上而輔成
君德致吾君為堯舜之君下而潤澤生民使斯民為
堯舜之民由是天道以清地道以寧風雨寒暑
順其時山嶽河海奠其居推而至於鳥獸草木
飛潛蠕動之属皆有以安其生而遂其性雍熈
泰和之治詎不匹休於虞周哉雖然
聖問之所及臣既略陳之矣而於終篇頗有獻焉臣
惟天下國家之本在身而身之主則一心耳心
之存否天下國家治忽之所由係焉故堯舜禹

punctuated: 以知皇上此心必欲得天下真才之用，而致治之效必欲躋于雍熈泰和之盛也。然虞、周聖人所以致此者，豈偶然哉？實由躬行以為本耳。皇上誠能取法虞、周，躬行教化以培養士類，則必益重師儒之選，敦崇仁義之教，而「成人有德，小子有造」之效可致矣；躬行道德以選舉人才，則必益嚴主司之權，務慎貢舉之法，而「黎獻共臣，野無遺賢」之效可必矣；由是立為定制以考課庶官，則必益擇銓衡之任，大明黜陟之典，而「百工惟時，庶官無曠」之效可期矣。夫如是，則賢能在職，君子盈朝，上而輔成君德，致吾君為堯、舜之君；下而潤澤生民，使斯民為堯、舜之民。由是天道以清，地道以寧，風雨寒暑順其時，山嶽河海奠其居，推而至於鳥獸、草木、飛潛蠕動之属，皆有以安其生而遂其性，雍熈泰和之治，詎不匹休於虞、周哉？雖然，聖問之所及，臣既略陳之矣，而於終篇頗有獻焉。臣惟天下國家之本在身，而身之主則一心耳。心之存否，天下國家治忽之所由係焉。故堯、舜、禹、
translation_en:
…thereby know that in this intention Your Majesty surely desires to obtain the service of true talent throughout the realm, and that in the efficacy of bringing about good governance You surely desire to ascend to the flourishing heights of harmonious peace and supreme concord. Yet how could it be by mere chance that the sages of Yu and Zhou achieved this? Truly, it was by taking personal practice as the foundation.

If Your Majesty can truly pattern Yourself after Yu and Zhou, personally practicing moral transformation in order to nurture the literati, then You will surely attach ever greater weight to the selection of teachers and Confucian scholars, and earnestly exalt the teachings of benevolence and righteousness; thus the efficacy of "grown men possessing virtue, and young ones making progress" can be achieved. If You personally practice morality and virtue in order to select men of talent, then You will surely enforce ever more strictly the authority of the chief examiners, and take care to be prudent in the laws of recommendation and examination; thus the efficacy of "the eminent among the black-haired people all serving as subjects, and no worthy left overlooked in the wilderness" can be assured. If from this You establish fixed regulations to evaluate the performance of the various officials, then You will surely be ever more selective in appointments to the offices of personnel evaluation, and greatly clarify the canons of demotion and promotion; thus the efficacy of "all the artisans timely in their work, and the various offices never left neglected" can be anticipated.

When it is like this, the worthy and capable will hold office and noble men will fill the court. Above, they will assist in perfecting the Sovereign's virtue, causing our Lord to become a ruler like Yao and Shun; below, they will enrich and benefit the living people, making these people become a people like those of Yao and Shun. Thereby the Way of Heaven will become clear and the Way of Earth tranquil; wind and rain, cold and heat will follow their proper seasons; mountains and peaks, rivers and seas will be settled in their proper places; and extending even to birds and beasts, grasses and trees, and creatures that fly, dive, or wriggle, all will have the means to rest secure in their lives and fulfill their natures. How then would a governance of harmonious peace and supreme concord not match the splendor of Yu and Zhou?

Even so, what Your Sacred Question touched upon, Your servant has already briefly set forth; yet at the conclusion of this essay I have something further to offer. Your servant reflects that the foundation of the empire and the state lies in the ruler's own person, and the master of the person is simply the one mind. Whether this mind is preserved or not is that upon which the order or neglect of the empire and the state depends. Therefore Yao, Shun, Yu,…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
湯文武隆古之聖君也猶兢兢業業以存此心
太甲成王商周之賢君也必困心衡慮以存此
心故皆能成至治於當時煥功德於萬世伏惟
皇上體帝王之要道以存心為出治之本則
聖德神功足以光昭
祖宗之鴻烈而
宗社生民之福將與天地相為悠久矣臣學識淺陋
叨奉
大對謹述直辭上塵
睿覽干冒
===
天威不勝悚懼之至臣謹對

punctuated: 湯、文、武，隆古之聖君也，猶兢兢業業以存此心；太甲、成王，商、周之賢君也，必困心衡慮以存此心。故皆能成至治於當時，煥功德於萬世。伏惟皇上體帝王之要道，以存心為出治之本，則聖德神功足以光昭祖宗之鴻烈，而宗社生民之福，將與天地相為悠久矣。臣學識淺陋，叨奉大對，謹述直辭，上塵睿覽。干冒天威，不勝悚懼之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: …Tang, Wen, and Wu were sage rulers of high antiquity, yet they still acted with cautious diligence to preserve this mind; Taijia and King Cheng were worthy rulers of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, and they necessarily distressed their minds and perplexed their thoughts to preserve this mind. Therefore, they were all able to achieve supreme governance in their own times and make their merits and virtues shine across ten thousand generations. Humbly, I pray that Your Majesty will embody the essential Way of the emperors and kings, taking the preservation of the mind as the root from which governance issues forth; then your sage virtue and divine achievement will suffice to gloriously manifest the grand accomplishments of the Imperial Ancestors, and the blessings of the ancestral altars and the living people will endure as long as heaven and earth. Your servant is of shallow learning and knowledge; having had the undeserved honor of responding to the Great Inquiry, I respectfully set forth my candid words to sully Your sagely perusal on high. Having offended Your heavenly majesty, I am overcome with the utmost fear and trepidation. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
臣黃諫
臣對臣惟人君圖治莫先於用賢而用賢之要
尤在於脩身能脩其身則明於知人而所用皆
賢由是有君有臣而政無不舉矣又何慮天下
國家之不治哉故堯舜禹湯文武所以致雍熈
泰和之盛者皆本諸此道也而漢唐宋之治效
不古若者庸非此道之未盡歟恭惟
陛下帝德廣運聖學緝熈以大有為之資居大有為
之位而行大有為之政誠近古以來所未有也
而猶不自滿足特進臣等於
===
廷降賜清問首舉求賢圖治之道以及虞周得人
之盛與夫漢唐宋治不逮古之由下詢草茅臣
有以知
陛下是心即堯舜稽于有衆清問下民之心湯文用
人惟己望道未見之心也臣雖不足上揆
淵衷敢不抒一得之愚以對揚
聖天子之明命乎臣聞書曰惟治亂在庶官官不及
私昵惟其能爵罔及惡德惟其賢誠以能則足
以任事賢則足以惇化是豈可以易而致哉良
由乎培養有素選舉有方考課之嚴明也

以任事賢則足以惇化是豈可以易而致哉良
由乎培養有素選舉有方考課之嚴明也
punctuated:
臣黃諫。

臣對：臣惟人君圖治，莫先於用賢，而用賢之要，尤在於脩身。能脩其身，則明於知人，而所用皆賢。由是有君有臣，而政無不舉矣，又何慮天下國家之不治哉？故堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武所以致雍熈泰和之盛者，皆本諸此道也；而漢、唐、宋之治效不古若者，庸非此道之未盡歟？恭惟陛下帝德廣運，聖學緝熈，以大有為之資，居大有為之位，而行大有為之政，誠近古以來所未有也。而猶不自滿足，特進臣等於廷，降賜清問，首舉求賢圖治之道，以及虞、周得人之盛，與夫漢、唐、宋治不逮古之由，下詢草茅。臣有以知陛下是心，即堯、舜稽于有衆、清問下民之心，湯、文用人惟己、望道未見之心也。臣雖不足上揆淵衷，敢不抒一得之愚，以對揚聖天子之明命乎？

臣聞《書》曰：「惟治亂在庶官。官不及私昵，惟其能；爵罔及惡德，惟其賢。」誠以能則足以任事，賢則足以惇化，是豈可以易而致哉？良由乎培養有素，選舉有方，考課之嚴明也。
translation_en:
Your servant Huang Jian 黃諫.

Your servant replies: Your servant reflects that when a ruler plans for good governance, nothing takes precedence over employing the worthy, and the essential key to employing the worthy lies above all in cultivating his own person. When he is able to cultivate his person, he is clear-sighted in knowing men, and all whom he employs are worthy. Consequently, there is both a true ruler and true ministers, and no affair of government fails to be carried out—what worry could there then be that the empire and the state would not be well governed? Thus, the means by which Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu brought about the flourishing of harmonious peace and great concord were all rooted in this Way. And as for the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties failing to match antiquity in the efficacy of their rule—was it not because they did not fully exhaust this Way?

Your servant reverently reflects that Your Majesty's imperial virtue operates far and wide, and Your sacred learning shines with continuous brightness. With the endowment for great achievements, You occupy a position for great achievements and carry out a governance of great achievements—truly something unseen since recent antiquity. Yet You still do not consider Yourself satisfied, and have specially summoned Your servants to the Court, graciously bestowing Your pure inquiries. First raising the Way of seeking the worthy and planning for governance, together with the flourishing of obtaining capable men in the Yu and Zhou periods and the reasons why the governance of Han, Tang, and Song fell short of antiquity, You have condescended to consult humble scholars from the countryside. By this Your servant knows that this mind of Your Majesty is none other than the mind of Yao and Shun in consulting the multitude and purely questioning the lower people, and the mind of Tang and King Wen in employing others as though from themselves and looking toward the Way as though not yet having seen it. Although Your servant is inadequate to fathom the depths of Your profound thoughts above, how could he dare not pour forth his humble understanding of a single point, so as to respond to and extol the illustrious mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven?

Your servant has heard that the Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Order and disorder lie with the multitudinous officials. Offices should not be given to private favorites, but only to the able; ranks of nobility should not be bestowed on men of evil virtue, but only on the worthy." Truly, because the able are sufficient to take charge of affairs and the worthy are sufficient to thicken moral transformation, how could this be easily achieved? It is indeed due to long-standing cultivation, proper methods of selection and recommendation, and strictness and clarity in performance evaluation.

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
聖朝混一以来首以甄陶士類養育人材為務故內建
國學以儲天下之賢外設郡邑學以育閭里之秀
豐其廩饌蠲其徭役其培養之素固與虞周之
敬敷式和同一道矣三年大比賓興賢能定解
額以取人汰浮文而務實有能有為舉蒙擢用
其選舉之方固與虞周明揚迪簡同一揆矣以
至三載一考定其殿最九載三考明其黜陟有
正官而各考所統有臺憲而分考所巡此其考
課之善又與虞周無二致矣是以內而經邦論
道者皆得其人外而承流宣化者舉獲其用又
===
何未盡得人哉然而知人之事自古為難人藏
其心不可測度其或百官有司未盡得人者誠
由任其責者教養有未善知人有未明而考覈
有未精耳稽諸三代以上若命契敷教以親百
姓命夔典樂以教胄子以至庠序學校之異其
設大學小學之異其教此唐虞三代培養人材
之有素可知矣舜有天下選於衆舉臯陶湯有
天下選於衆舉伊尹以至大比賓興有其制鄉
舉里選有其法此唐虞三代選舉人才之有方
可見矣至於三載考績三考黜陟幽明嵗終考

translation_en:
Since Our Sacred Dynasty unified the realm, it has made its primary task the molding of scholars and the nurturing of men of talent. Thus, at the capital it established the Directorate of Education to store up the worthy men of the empire, and in the provinces it set up prefectural and county schools to nurture the finest talents of the villages and neighborhoods, generously providing their stipends and food and exempting them from corvée labor. Its foundational cultivation of talent truly shares the same Way as the reverent dissemination of instruction under Yu [Shun] and the harmonious modeling of conduct under the Zhou. Every three years at the grand triennial comparison, the worthy and able are presented as honored guests; quotas for forwarding candidates are fixed for selecting men, superficial rhetoric is weeded out in favor of substance, and all who possess ability and accomplishment receive promotion and employment. Its methods of selection and recommendation truly follow the same principles as the open promotion of the lowly under Yu and the guiding and choosing of officials under the Zhou. Furthermore, there is an evaluation every three years to determine their lowest and highest merits, and three evaluations over nine years to make clear their demotions and promotions; principal officials each evaluate their own subordinates, and Censorate and Surveillance Commission officials separately evaluate the jurisdictions they tour. The excellence of its system of performance evaluation is likewise no different from that of Yu and the Zhou. Therefore, at court those who order the state and deliberate on the Way are all the right men, and in the provinces those who transmit the ruler's grace and spread moral transformation all fulfill their functions—how could there still be any failure to obtain the right men in full?

Nevertheless, knowing men has been difficult since antiquity, for men conceal their hearts and cannot be fathomed. If among the hundred officials and various functionaries the right men have not yet been fully obtained, it is truly because those charged with this responsibility have not yet perfected their instruction and nurturing, have not yet been discerning in knowing men, and have not yet been precise in examining and verifying performance. If we examine the Three Dynasties and earlier: X契 (Xie) was commanded to spread the Five Teachings so that the hundred surnames would be affectionate, and Kui 夔 was commanded to direct music in order to teach the sons of state, down to the differing establishments of village and state schools (xiang, xu, xue, and xiao) and the differing curricula of Greater Learning and Lesser Learning—from this, the foundational cultivation of talent in the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties can be known. When Shun possessed the empire, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Gao Yao 臯陶; when Tang 湯 possessed the empire, he selected from among the multitude and raised up Yi Yin 伊尹; down to having established institutions for the triennial comparison and guest-presentation of talent, and having set methods for district recommendation and village selection—from this, the methodical selection of talent in the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties can be seen. As for evaluating achievements every three years and demoting theindolent and promoting the enlightened after three evaluations, and at the end of the year examining…

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
歲會月終考月要日終考日成大宰掌大計之
制小宰有六善之法此唐虞三代考課之嚴明
又何如哉故唐虞之時九德咸事俊乂在官成
周之世濟濟多士秉文之德雖由行是三者實
本乎堯舜克明俊德慎厥身脩文武聰明齊聖
克慎明德以致之也是則唐虞三代之所以得
人成治何莫不本於脩身也哉三代而下言治
者莫漢唐宋若也觀漢文帝謙讓未遑賈誼以
忠愛之誠陳治安一策卒不能用止於長沙傅
而已武帝好大喜功董子以王佐之才陳天人
===
三策卒不能行終於江都相而已當時雖有賢
良茂才之舉三科六條之制徒尚虛名而不求
其實此漢之治所以止於漢也唐太宗急於功
利雖有禮樂之問而房杜汗浹無對憲宗惑於
異端韓愈以名世大儒力排佛老而竟貶潮州
當時雖有進士明經之科四善二十七最之制
亦徒尚文具而不務其本此唐之治所以止於
唐也以至宋太祖太宗之創業真宗仁宗之守
成固皆有志於治柰何後世之主耽於嗜好心
術不明好惡用舍多失其當而王安石吕惠卿

三策卒不能行終於江都相而已當時雖有賢
良茂才之舉三科六條之制徒尚虛名而不求
其實此漢之治所以止於漢也唐太宗急於功
利雖有禮樂之問而房杜汗浹無對憲宗惑於
異端韓愈以名世大儒力排佛老而竟貶潮州
當時雖有進士明經之科四善二十七最之制
亦徒尚文具而不務其本此唐之治所以止於
唐也以至宋太祖太宗之創業真宗仁宗之守
成固皆有志於治柰何後世之主耽於嗜好心
術不明好惡用舍多失其當而王安石呂惠卿
punctuated:
歲會，月終考月要，日終考日成，大宰掌大計之制，小宰有六善之法，此唐、虞、三代考課之嚴明又何如哉！故唐、虞之時，九德咸事，俊乂在官；成周之世，濟濟多士，秉文之德。雖由行是三者，實本乎堯、舜克明俊德、慎厥身脩，文、武聰明齊聖、克慎明德以致之也。是則唐、虞、三代之所以得人成治，何莫不本於脩身也哉！
三代而下，言治者莫漢、唐、宋若也。觀漢文帝謙讓未遑，賈誼以忠愛之誠，陳《治安》一策，卒不能用，止於長沙傅而已；武帝好大喜功，董子以王佐之才，陳天人三策，卒不能行，終於江都相而已。當時雖有賢良、茂才之舉，三科、六條之制，徒尚虛名而不求其實，此漢之治所以止於漢也。唐太宗急於功利，雖有禮樂之問，而房、杜汗浹無對；憲宗惑於異端，韓愈以名世大儒，力排佛、老，而竟貶潮州。當時雖有進士、明經之科，四善、二十七最之制，亦徒尚文具而不務其本，此唐之治所以止於唐也。以至宋太祖、太宗之創業，真宗、仁宗之守成，固皆有志於治；柰何後世之主耽於嗜好，心術不明，好惡用舍多失其當，而王安石、吕惠卿、
translation_en:
… the annual totals at the end of the year, examining the monthly summaries at the end of the month, and examining the daily completions at the end of the day; the system whereby the Grand宰 (Grand Counselor, Dazai) took charge of the grand triennial evaluation, and the method of the six virtues held by the Junior Counselor (Xiaozai)—how strict and clear indeed was this evaluation of officials in the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties! Therefore, in the time of Tang and Yu, men of all nine virtues served in affairs and eminent talents were in office; in the age of flourishing Zhou, thenumerous gentlemen were dignified and upheld the virtue of King Wen. Although this resulted from practicing these three things, in reality it was rooted in Yao and Shun being able to make illustrious their lofty virtue and being careful in their personal cultivation, and in Kings Wen and Wu being intelligent, sagely, and able to be cautious of their luminous virtue so as to bring this about. Thus, how could the means by which Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties obtained men of talent and achieved good governance not be rooted in personal cultivation!

From the Three Dynasties downward, among those who speak of good governance, none can match Han, Tang, and Song. Observe how Emperor Wen of Han was modest and deferential, claiming he had no leisure yet for institutional reforms; Jia Yi 賈誼, out of loyal and affectionate sincerity, presented his single Policy on Peace and Order (Zhi'an ce), yet in the end it could not be used, and he ended up merely as Grand Tutor of Changsha (Changsha fu). Emperor Wu loved grandeur and delighted in martial exploits; Master Dong [Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒], with the talent of a kingly assistant, presented his three policy essays on Heaven and Man, yet in the end they could not be put into practice, and he finished merely as Chancellor of Jiangdu (Jiangdu xiang). At that time, although there were recommendations of the Worthy and Excellent (xianliang) and Flourishing Talent (maocai), and the systems of the Three Categories (sanke) and Six Articles (liutiao), they merely esteemed empty names without seeking the reality. This is why the governance of Han went no further than being that of Han. Emperor Taizong of Tang was eager for quick success and profit; although he asked questions about rites and music, Fang [Fang Xuanling 房玄齡] and Du [Du Ruhui 杜如晦] weredrenched in sweat and had no reply. Emperor Xianzong was deluded by heterodoxies; Han Yu 韓愈, as a great Confucian renowned in his generation, vigorously rejected Buddhism and Daoism, yet was ultimately banished to Chaozhou. At that time, although there were the examination categories of Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi) and Classicist (mingjing), and the system of the Four Virtues (sishan) and Twenty-Seven Qualifications (ershiqi zui) for evaluating officials, they likewise merely esteemed outward formalities without attending to the fundamental root. This is why the governance of Tang went no further than being that of Tang. Coming down to the founding of the dynasty by Emperors Taizu and Taizong of Song, and the preservation of the heritage by Emperors Zhenzong and Renzong, they assuredly all had the ambition to achieve good governance. Yet what could be done when the rulers of later generations indulged in their personal predilections, the workings of their minds were not clear, their likes and dislikes, employments and dismissals mostly lost what was proper, and the likes of Wang Anshi 王安石, Lü Huiqing 呂惠卿, …

title: 正統七年進士登科錄
text:
曾布章子厚之徒相繼為用更立新法排斥正
人雖有濂洛關建之大儒皆不獲見用於時欲
治效之復古亦不可得矣是則漢唐宋之君於
取人以身之道槩乎有所未至也今
陛下欲脩身以隆治化要當舎漢唐宋而法帝王之
盛可也夫帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於身
身既脩矣則於學校之政選舉之方考課之法
無施而不可矣此臣惓惓以脩身一語為終篇
獻者無他盖以
陛下之所期者在得人以為安民之本臣之望於
===
陛下者在脩身以為取人之則也孔子曰為政在人
取人以身脩身以道脩道以仁是道與仁又脩
身之要也伏願
陛下始終以此仁此道而脩其身則君德以成皇極
以建其於天下之賢才培養之所成選舉之所
得而考課之所激勸皆真才實德之士而致治
之效足以臻雍熈泰和之盛尚何俾唐虞三代
專美於前哉芻蕘之辭直述以對惟
陛下少垂
睿覽不勝幸甚臣謹對

punctuated: 曾布、章子厚之徒相繼為用，更立新法，排斥正人；雖有濂、洛、關、建之大儒，皆不獲見用於時，欲治效之復古，亦不可得矣。是則漢、唐、宋之君，於取人以身之道，槩乎有所未至也。今陛下欲脩身以隆治化，要當舎漢、唐、宋而法帝王之盛可也。夫帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於身。身既脩矣，則於學校之政、選舉之方、考課之法，無施而不可矣。此臣惓惓以脩身一語為終篇獻者，無他，盖以陛下之所期者，在得人以為安民之本；臣之望於陛下者，在脩身以為取人之則也。孔子曰：「為政在人，取人以身，脩身以道，脩道以仁。」是道與仁，又脩身之要也。伏願陛下始終以此仁、此道而脩其身，則君德以成，皇極以建；其於天下之賢才，培養之所成、選舉之所得，而考課之所激勸，皆真才實德之士，而致治之效，足以臻雍熈泰和之盛，尚何俾唐、虞、三代專美於前哉！芻蕘之辭，直述以對，惟陛下少垂睿覽，不勝幸甚。臣謹對。
translation_en: … Zeng Bu 曾布, and Zhang Zihou 章子厚 were employed one after another, altering and establishing the New Policies and ostracizing upright men. Even though there were the great Confucian scholars of Lian 濂, Luo 洛, Guan 關, and Jian 建, none of them succeeded in being employed in their time; thus, even if one wished for the efficacy of governance to return to antiquity, it could not be attained. Therefore, the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, in the Way of selecting men by means of one's own person, all fell short in some respect. Now, if Your Majesty wishes to cultivate Your person in order to exalt transformative governance, You must set aside the Han, Tang, and Song, and model Yourself on the flourishing ages of the Five Emperors and Three Kings. Now, the governance of the Emperors and Kings is rooted in the Way, and the Way of the Emperors and Kings is rooted in the person. Once the person is cultivated, then with regard to the administration of schools, the methods of selection and recommendation, and the laws of performance evaluation, there is nothing to which it can be applied without success. The reason your servant earnestly offers this single phrase, "cultivating the person," throughout this entire essay is none other than this: what Your Majesty hopes for lies in obtaining men as the foundation for pacifying the people, while what your servant hopes for from Your Majesty lies in cultivating Your person as the standard for selecting men. Confucius said: "Governance lies in men; men are selected by means of one's own person; the person is cultivated by means of the Way; the Way is cultivated by means of benevolence." Thus, the Way and benevolence are, in turn, the essentials for cultivating the person. Your servant humbly prays that Your Majesty will from beginning to end cultivate Your person by means of this benevolence and this Way. Then the ruler's virtue will be accomplished and the august standard of perfection will be established. With regard to the worthy talents of the realm, those brought to maturity through nurturing, those obtained through selection and recommendation, and those stimulated and encouraged through performance evaluation will all be scholars of true talent and substantial virtue. The efficacy of achieving good governance will suffice to reach the flourishing of harmonious peace and supreme concord—how then could Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and the Three Dynasties be allowed to monopolize the glory of the past! In the humble words of a grass-cutter and firewood-gatherer, I have stated my reply directly; I only pray that Your Majesty will deign to cast Your imperial gaze upon it, which would be fortunate beyond measure. Your servant respectfully replies.
